channel.title: Said & Checked: Trade and Tariffs — AskAmerica
channel.description: What officeholders said each day about Trade and Tariffs, and which statements government data supports, contradicts or rules out.

item.title: Said & Checked, Trade and Tariffs, 2026-11-20: none false or contradicted, 4 unsettled (Chuck Schumer, Tim Kaine)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Chuck Schumer, U.S. Senator: “Nothing to stop the flow of fentanyl, nothing to keep our most advanced chips out of the PLA's hands, nothing to curb Chinese espionage into our companies, nothing to protect American manufacturers, nothing to end Russia's criminal invasion of Ukraine,…” Unsettled. Fox News's account of the declaration and readouts describes commitments on strategic stability, nuclear risk, refined-petroleum supply and international institutions, with none on the listed subjects, but the White House, Chinese and Russian texts themselves could not be read.
  • Tim Kaine, U.S. Senator: “The average tariff rate on goods coming into the United States for most of post-World War II has been 2 percent; the average tariff rate now is 12 percent” Unsettled. USITC data in AskAmerica's warehouse show duties collected at about 1% to 2.4% of import value from 2008 to 2024, rising to 7.6% in 2025; earlier post-war decades are not covered, 2026 import totals are not yet loaded, and a 12% figure appears only in statutory-rate estimates that were not read.
  • Tim Kaine, U.S. Senator: “President Trump's decision under emergency powers--not by vote of Congress, not with the demand or really the approval of Congress--to put tariffs on virtually any product coming into the United States.” Unsettled. The broad tariffs were imposed by executive orders under emergency declarations using the International Emergency Economic Powers Act, with no congressional vote, and the Supreme Court held in Learning Resources v. Trump (Feb. 20, 2026) that the law does not authorize tariffs; replacement tariffs reportedly rest on a trade statute Congress delegated earlier, which was not read.

item.title: Said & Checked, Trade and Tariffs, 2026-11-19: none false or contradicted, 1 unsettled (Donald Trump)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Donald Trump, President of the United States: “Reported as: He said after their meeting that the two nations had reached a trade deal on Wednesday, though he had also said last year that an agreement had been reached.” Unsettled. Neither the White House statements page (current through Nov. 17) nor USTR's press releases (current through Nov. 18) carried a U.S.-Philippines trade document, and neither government has said no deal was reached; an AP report dates a signing to Tuesday, Nov. 17. Only verbal accounts of the agreement were found.

item.title: Said & Checked, Trade and Tariffs, 2026-11-18: none false or contradicted, 2 unsettled (Donald Trump, Rob Wittman)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Donald Trump, President of the United States: “Reported as: He said after their meeting that the two nations had reached a trade deal on Wednesday, though he had also said last year that an agreement had been reached.” Unsettled. No official document from either government announcing a U.S.-Philippines trade agreement on Nov. 18 was found; the White House said only that it involves Manila buying more energy and farm products. A news report says Marcos's office described an 'understanding on areas of economic cooperation' and the Philippine ambassador said nothing was signed.
  • Rob Wittman, U.S. Representative from Virginia: “China controls 70 percent of rare earth mining, 90 percent of rare earth separation and processing, and 93 percent of rare earth magnet manufacturing.” Unsettled. AskAmerica's USGS mineral data put China at 270,000 of 390,000 metric tons of world rare-earth mine production in 2025 (69%) and 71% in 2024, matching 'about 70%'. No official source for the 90% processing or 93% magnet shares could be read; IEA figures seen only in search summaries are about 85-91% and 94%.

item.title: Said & Checked, Trade and Tariffs, 2026-11-15: none false or contradicted, 1 unsettled (Mike Pence)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Mike Pence, Former Vice President of the United States: “not only broad-based tariffs on friend and foe alike, but nationalizing 41 American businesses, in part, price controls on pharmaceuticals and credit cards.” Unsettled. No agency publishes a list of federal ownership stakes in companies. A 24/7 Wall St. article says private tallies run from 30 to 43, so 41 is within their range but is not an official figure, and the stakes are minority holdings. No primary document on price controls for pharmaceuticals or credit cards was read.
